evidence.note: CONFIRMED: merge_log's window must resolve the main BRANCH (refs/heads/main), not the bare 'main'. Empirical probe: in a repo with branch refs/heads/main (tip = merge T1) and a tag refs/tags/main at an older base, 'git rev-parse --verify --quiet main' returned the TAG sha (3643b2a2) while 'refs/heads/main' returned the branch sha (0697e2bc) — git resolves refs/tags before refs/heads. The bare name therefore anchors the recall window to a stale point and drops main's real merges; pinning refs/heads/main fixes it. Regression test test_merge_log_uses_the_main_branch_not_a_tag_named_main added (fails on bare 'main', passes on 'refs/heads/main').

Test-only change to tests/test_testselect_recall.py (in the item's globs). Follows rule r-small-files (one file), r-gemini-key-load (load key before review), r-secrets, r-log-is-the-state. No README/golden/snapshot files needed.

chunk_findings.detail: The blind-exclusion logic still builds one global set of blind test ids from all `residual` entries across all replays and then removes any id in that set from the flattened `lost` list, without per-merge provenance. This diff only changes the `merge_log` anchor and adds a new tag test; it does not fix the global filter. Concrete failure: if replay of merge A has residual `tests/test_x.py (blind: show failed)` and replay of merge B has `tests/test_x.py` in `lost` because the selector genuinely missed a changed source, the id is already in the global blind set, so it is dropped from `unexpected`; the recall test passes despite a real selector regression in merge B.

chunk_findings.detail: The diff fixes the `merge_log` anchor and adds the tag-shadow test but leaves the blind-filtering logic unchanged. The blind filter is still computed as a global set of test ids from all `residual` entries and then applied to every id in the flattened `lost` list without per-merge provenance. This hides real selector misses whenever a test id is blind on one replay and genuinely lost on another. Example: results contain one merge with residual `tests/test_x.py (blind: show failed)` and another merge whose `lost` includes `tests/test_x.py` from a real selector miss; after flattening, `tests/test_x.py` is filtered out of `unexpected` by the unrelated blind entry, so the recall test passes despite the regression. The new `refs/heads/main` anchor check does not answer this.
